transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Samira Khan (Aurora CTO), Devon Lee (Aurora Lead ML Eng), Priyanka Rao (Aurora Infra)

Summary:
Aurora is exploring Redwood's self-serve API to get to first request quickly for a feature flagging assistant and a doc-search prototype. Primary concerns: data residency, KMS/integration, latency targets (p50 < 200ms for short queries), and predictability of cost. They asked about Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and want a sandbox to verify latency/cost. Agreed next steps to provision free credits and schedule a deeper SE-led technical session for private deployment sizing.

Topics:
- Quickstart time-to-first-token and sandbox flow
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: tradeoffs and timelines
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, data retention
- Cost controls: batching, quantization, token accounting
- Success criteria and pilot scope (qps, latency, datasets)

Action items (auto-gen, also in metadata):
- Maya to run quick perf estimate and run a small inference sim using Aurora sample prompts
- Jordan to share trial/project provisioning instructions and the security packet link
- Aurora to share qps, dataset sizes, and any regulatory constraints

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh i'm jordan from redwood, i run the dev motion here, with maya — she is our solutions eng who will run the tech bits. how's everyone doing?
[00:11] Samira Khan: good, thanks. busy week but excited to finally talk through this. we got your note about free credits and wanted to understand how fast we can get something live.
[00:21] Jordan Patel: totally. the quick path is signup, create a sandbox project, we provision credits and you can call the hosted API within minutes. time-to-first-token usually under 15 minutes for dev flows, if you have a sample prompt we can run right away.
[00:35] Devon Lee: quick q — when you say hosted, is that shared infra? we have to know about PII and storage.
[00:41] Maya Chen: yeah so hosted is our managed api, data in transit encrypted, option to disable logging and we have retention controls. for regulated data we recommend either Dedicated or Private; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and isolation within our tenancy, Private puts the control plane inside your VPC.
[01:02] Priyanka Rao: what about kms integration? we use a corporate hsm and prefer envelope encryption.
[01:08] Maya Chen: we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments, for dedicated we support customer-managed keys via our KMS bridge — it's in the security doc, i'll paste the link in follow-up: https://redwood.ai/docs/security (note: link shared).
[01:22] Samira Khan: okay, good. also latency — we need p50 < 200ms for short classification calls (~8 tokens). is that realistic on hosted?
[01:31] Jordan Patel: depends on model size and seq length; small curated models we host can hit those numbers in edge regions. if you need strict p50s at scale, Dedicated with reserved pools is the more predictable path. but we can prototype on hosted to measure real numbers quickly.
[01:47] Devon Lee: and cost — our finance will push back if we can't bound spend. are there tooling to limit runaway calls?
[01:55] Maya Chen: yep, rate limits, per-project quotas, and token caps. Plus our Optimize tooling can suggest batching/quant settings to reduce per-token cost. We also expose token-level billing so you can map cost to routes.
[02:11] Samira Khan: nice. for the quickstart, what's the onboarding flow — do devs need anything special?
[02:16] Jordan Patel: nothing special: signup, API key, SDK or REST, example curl. we give starter templates for node/python, and a playground. if you want SSO for the console, we support SAML/IdP setup for team onboarding.
[02:31] Devon Lee: sample prompts — we'll share a small set, ~300 prompts across intent classification + doc retrieval simulation. can you run a batch to estimate token usage and latency?
[02:41] Maya Chen: absolutely, if you drop them into a shared drive or paste a small CSV we can run a short perf sim against hosted models to give you p50/p95 and token counts.
[02:52] Samira Khan: what about private on-prem? timeline and lift?
[02:56] Maya Chen: private is more involved — customer-managed control plane, network peering, KMS, air-gapped options if needed. typical pilot is 6-12 weeks for on-prem depending on procurement and infra readiness; Dedicated is faster — usually weeks to reserve capacity and onboard.
[03:15] Jordan Patel: and to add, for most teams we recommend "hosted pilot" first to validate prompts and UX, then Dedicated or Private for production with SLA.
[03:26] Priyanka Rao: security checklist — do you have SOC2 / ISO docs and an audit log export?
[03:31] Maya Chen: yes, SOC2 Type II, we also have PCI adjacency notes. audit logs are available for Dedicated/Private with export to your SIEM; hosted has reporting windows and audit trails — i'll link the packet.
[03:47] Samira Khan: good — please send that.
[03:49] Jordan Patel: will do. we'll also include an abbreviated runbook for the sandbox and steps to turn off logging for dev tokens.
[03:58] Devon Lee: curious about model variants — can we pin a version and have automatic fallback if a model is noisy?
[04:05] Maya Chen: yes, rollout policies let you pin versions, canary traffic split, and fallback to a compatible variant or quantized model. that helps resilience if one zone has issues.
[04:18] Samira Khan: on pricing, how predictable is Dedicated vs hosted?
[04:22] Jordan Patel: Hosted is usage-based (tokens/embeddings), Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit that gives predictable unit economics. We can run a cost projection against your sample workload.
[04:34] Devon Lee: can you do a quick example — say 2k qps ephemeral?
[04:39] Maya Chen: for 2k qps you likely need Dedicated GPU pools, autoscaling rules, and a burst policy. we'll need details on request size and concurrency to size correctly. we'll protobuf a rough estimate in the follow-up.
[04:56] Samira Khan: timeline — if we like the hosted pilot, say we start next week, how soon can we have an SE deep-dive for private sizing?
[05:04] Jordan Patel: we can schedule SE deep-dive within 7-10 days after you approve; Maya will lead that.
[05:11] Maya Chen: yep, i'll prepare an agenda — infra checklist, network topology, KMS, and perf targets.
[05:18] Samira Khan: ok perfect.
[05:21] [longer stretch of discussion — details on sample prompts and data share method]
[07:10] Devon Lee: one more Q: does redwood provide any client side caching / kv cache guidance for conversational memory? we run a chat feature in the roadmap.
[07:19] Maya Chen: we do recommend prefix & KV cache patterns and have SDK helpers; for Redwood runtime we support KV cache and auto-sharding to reduce duplicate computation. we'll share code snippets.
[07:31] Samira Khan: are there any gotchas with token counting and embeddings? we use embeddings for semantic search and worried about hidden costs.
[07:39] Jordan Patel: embeddings have different units in billing, and also there's an index storage cost if you use our managed vector store. you can self-host indices and keep inference with Redwood to optimize costs.
[07:53] Priyanka Rao: regarding compliance — do you support data residency in eu-west region only? we have eu-only customers.
[07:59] Maya Chen: yes, we have region restrictions and can restrict projects to eu-west or customer VPC for Private. Dedicated can also be provisioned in specific regions.
[08:10] Samira Khan: excellent. any blockers from our side to start the quickstart?
[08:14] Samira Khan: i mean besides approvals — we'll need the sandbox and a stub invoice for procurement maybe.
[08:19] Jordan Patel: we'll include a one-page procurement note and invoice sample.
[08:24] Jordan Patel: okay let's recap the agreed next steps — provisioning credits, perf sim, security packet, schedule deep-dive.
[08:33] Maya Chen: i'll run the perf sim once we get the CSV, and i'll include p50/p95 and token counts.
[08:40] Devon Lee: we'll share the prompts and traffic patterns by friday.
[08:44] Samira Khan: sounds good. thanks, everyone.
[08:47] Jordan Patel: thanks, wrap-up: i'll send an email with links to docs: security packet, quickstart guide (https://redwood.ai/docs/quickstart), and the sandbox invite.
[08:58] Meeting end (recording stops)
